business_problem: Rokid needed a better way to run GPU-intensive AR guidance services for digital-culture experiences. The company wanted demand-based GPU elasticity, faster release and rollback, better control of burst capacity, and a standard serverless pattern that could support real-time scene-experience services without a maze of Kubernetes objects and manual tuning.
solution_summary: Rokid used Alibaba Cloud ACK with Knative to serverless-ize the online service layer behind its AR exhibition-guidance applications. Knative gives the team request- and concurrency-based scaling, traffic-based gray release, rollback, and multi-version management so new application versions can ship without rebuilding a large set of Kubernetes primitives for each rollout. To reduce the lag of conventional HPA scaling, Rokid also adopted ACK's AHPA prediction so pods can be prepared ahead of expected traffic increases rather than only after metrics cross a static threshold. The deployment mixes ECS and ECI capacity and applies a custom ResourcePolicy so normal load prefers long-lived ECS capacity while burst traffic spills into ECI, and scale-down releases ECI first. Together, those controls let Rokid pursue GPU efficiency, faster delivery, and more deterministic real-time service behavior for AR scene experiences.

solution_components.name: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK)
solution_components.role: Hosts the serverless AI application environment that runs Rokid's online AR services.

solution_components.name: Knative
solution_components.role: Adds request-driven scaling, multi-version delivery, and traffic-based rollout controls for GPU-backed services.

solution_components.name: AHPA
solution_components.role: Predicts upcoming demand and pre-scales pods before traffic surges hit the service.

solution_components.name: Elastic Container Instance (ECI)
solution_components.role: Supplies burst container capacity when request spikes exceed baseline resources.

data_flow: AR scene-experience requests enter Knative services on ACK, where traffic levels drive scaling and version-routing behavior. AHPA predicts capacity needs ahead of spikes, while ResourcePolicy determines whether workloads land on ECS or ECI resources before responses are returned to location-aware AR clients.
business_outcome: Rokid improved rollout speed and demand responsiveness for AI-backed AR services while keeping GPU use closer to actual traffic. The company can now gray-release or roll back versions more easily, respond to burst demand with mixed ECS and ECI capacity, and run the online service layer on a more standard cloud-native serverless pattern.
metrics: products are used in 80+ countries and regions
AHPA plans capacity across 1440 minutes per day
architecture_clues: Rokid uses request and concurrency signals, not raw GPU-utilization thresholds, as the main elasticity trigger for online AI services.
AHPA is layered on top of Knative to pre-warm capacity before forecast traffic spikes arrive.
ResourcePolicy makes ECS the preferred baseline and ECI the burst tier so scale-in behavior remains deterministic.
